faqs.q: What is the Ball Check Valve, Ductile Iron, for Wastewater and what is it used for?
faqs.a: The Ball Check Valve, Ductile Iron, for Wastewater is a ductile iron ball check valve designed to EN 12334, used for sewage, sludge and wastewater pumping. It is listed in DN32 to DN400 (1-1/4" to 16") and PN10, PN16; Class 125/150. A rubber-coated ball rolls out of the flow path when the pump runs and back onto the seat when it stops; with no shaft or bushing there is nothing for rags and fibres to wrap around, and the ball cleans itself as it rotates.

faqs.q: How do I read the part numbers in the ductile iron ball check valve size table, such as IH-PV-WBC-PN10-0200?
faqs.a: In the ductile iron ball check valve size table the last four digits of the part number are the size in inches times 100 and the class code sits before them. IH-PV-WBC-PN10-0200 is 2" (DN50) in PN10, and IH-PV-WBC-PN10-0600 is 6" (DN150) in PN10.

faqs.q: What sizes and pressure classes does the Ball Check Valve, Ductile Iron, for Wastewater come in?
faqs.a: The Ball Check Valve, Ductile Iron, for Wastewater is published in DN32 to DN400 (1-1/4" to 16"), in PN10, PN16; Class 125/150. The size table lists 10 standard size and class combinations. Check size, class and end connection against the piping specification before you enquire.

faqs.a: The ductile iron ball check valve table gives lengths by size and class; in PN10 the face-to-face length is 200 mm at 2" (DN50), 400 mm at 6" (DN150) and 900 mm at 16" (DN400). The table lists lengths in millimetres; check the full row for the size and class you need.

faqs.a: Body material for the ductile iron ball check valve is ductile iron, cast iron; carbon steel, stainless steel, duplex and super duplex on request. Construction: rubber-coated ball, top cover. Tell us the fluid and temperature when you enquire so we confirm the material.

faqs.q: What standards does the Ball Check Valve, Ductile Iron, for Wastewater meet and what documents come with it?
faqs.a: The ductile iron ball check valve is designed to EN 12334. Testing: shell and seat tests to EN 12266-1 / API 598. Material certificates and the pressure-test record are supplied with the valve, and third-party inspection and extra tests are added when the order specifies them.

faqs.q: What end connections and operator options does the Ball Check Valve, Ductile Iron, for Wastewater have?
faqs.a: End connections on the ductile iron ball check valve are flanged to EN 1092-2 or ASME B16.1 / B16.5, RF or FF. It is self-acting, so it needs no operator.

faqs.q: Can the ductile iron ball check valve be installed vertically, and is it suitable for clean water?
faqs.a: It can be installed vertically with flow upward, though horizontal installation is most common. It works on clean water, but its advantage is on sewage and sludge; clean-water lines usually use swing or silent checks.

faqs.q: Why is a ball check valve used for sewage and sludge pumping?
faqs.a: The rubber-coated ball rolls out of the flow path when the pump runs and back onto the seat when it stops. With no shaft or bushing there is nothing for rags and fibres to wrap around, and the ball cleans itself as it rotates, which is why the valve is used for sewage, sludge and wastewater pumping.

faqs.q: How does the ball check valve differ from the silent check and swing check valves?
faqs.a: The ball check has a rubber-coated ball as its only moving part and suits solids-laden wastewater, while the [swing check valve](/p/waterworks-swing-check-valve) is the general-purpose type and the [silent check valve](/p/silent-check-valve-ductile-iron) closes on a spring before flow reverses for clean-water pump discharges. Choose the ball check where rags and fibres are present.

faqs.q: What is the Double Orifice Air Release Valve, Types A, B and C and what is it used for?
faqs.a: The Double Orifice Air Release Valve, Types A, B and C is a double orifice air release valve designed to EN 1074-4, AWWA C512, used for water transmission and distribution mains. It is listed in DN40 to DN300 (1-1/2" to 12") and PN10, PN16; Class 125/150. A double orifice valve vents large volumes of air as the main fills, admits air as it drains to stop vacuum collapse, and releases small pockets continuously while the main is under pressure.

faqs.a: Fit them at every high point, at changes of gradient, at long horizontal runs (every few hundred metres) and downstream of pumps and isolating valves. A double orifice valve vents large volumes of air as the main fills and admits air as it drains, so it protects against vacuum collapse.

faqs.a: In the ductile iron Y strainer size table the last four digits of the part number are the size in inches times 100 and the class code sits before them. IH-PV-WYS-PN16-0050 is 1/2" (DN15) in PN16, and IH-PV-WYS-PN25-0150 is 1-1/2" (DN40) in PN25.

faqs.q: What pressure and temperature is the Y Strainer, Ductile Iron, Flanged, DN15 to DN500 rated for?

faqs.q: What materials is the Y Strainer, Ductile Iron, Flanged, DN15 to DN500 made from?
faqs.a: Body material for the ductile iron Y strainer is ductile iron, cast iron; carbon steel, stainless steel, duplex and super duplex on request. Construction: angled screen leg, bolted cover. Tell us the fluid and temperature when you enquire so we confirm the material.

faqs.q: What standards does the Y Strainer, Ductile Iron, Flanged, DN15 to DN500 meet and what documents come with it?
faqs.a: The ductile iron Y strainer is designed to EN 12266-1 testing. Testing: shell and seat tests to EN 12266-1 / API 598. Material certificates and the pressure-test record are supplied with the valve, and third-party inspection and extra tests are added when the order specifies them.

faqs.q: What end connections and operator options does the Y Strainer, Ductile Iron, Flanged, DN15 to DN500 have?
faqs.a: End connections on the ductile iron Y strainer are flanged to EN 1092-2 or ASME B16.1 / B16.5, RF or FF. Give us the flange standard and facing (raised or flat face) of the mating pipework when you enquire, so the drilling matches.

faqs.q: What mesh size does the flanged ductile iron Y strainer use, and how is it cleaned?
faqs.a: Perforation is typically 1.5 to 3 mm for water mains and finer for meters and control valves, so tell us what the strainer protects. Clean it by opening the blow-off to flush, or by isolating the line and removing the cover to take out the screen.

faqs.q: What does a Y strainer protect on a water system?
faqs.a: It catches debris, scale and sediment ahead of pumps, control valves, meters and heat exchangers. Flow passes through a stainless screen held in the angled leg, and the solids collect there to be flushed through the drain plug or removed with the cover.

faqs.q: How does the Y strainer differ from the other waterworks valves in the range?
faqs.a: The Y strainer is not a shut-off or check valve: it only filters, through a stainless screen in an angled leg, and has no operator. It goes ahead of a valve such as the [resilient seated gate valve](/p/resilient-seated-gate-valve-ductile-iron) or a pump to keep debris out of the seat. It is listed DN15 to DN500.
